newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan evacuates 400 from strife-torn Cambodia.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan evacuates 400 from strife-torn Cambodia.

text.p: Taiwan on Thursday airlifted 400 of its citizens out of Cambodia, and urged all Taiwanese still in the strife-torn state to leave as soon as possible.
All three Vietnam Airline flights chartered by Taipei for the evacuation arrived safely in Ho Chi Minh City in Vietnam, the foreign ministry said.

Of the 400 evacuees, 57 returned late on Thursday to Taipei on a regular passenger flight by Taiwan's China Airlines. Two more flights by Taiwan's EVA Airways would carry the remaining people home later in the day, the ministry said.
"We will continue to serve our people in Cambodia in case they want to leave," Vice Foreign Minister Chen Chien-jen said.
"We do not recommend people staying in Cambodia, because the situation is still not very stable," Chen said.
Thailand and Singapore also have airlifted hundreds of their nationals from Cambodia. The United States has said it would be pulling out about 40 diplomats and dependants.
Australia said it would begin evacuation on Friday.
Cambodia recognises Taiwan's rival, communist China, and has no diplomatic ties with Taipei. But Taiwan ranks among the top foreign investors in Cambodia's fragile economy.
Flights from the Cambodian capital Phnom Penh resumed on Wednesday, four days after weekend fighting in Phnom Penh and elsewhere closed the capital's airport.
